newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana aluminium mill looks for strategic investors.
newsitem.headline: Ghana aluminium mill looks for strategic investors.

text.p: Ghana's Aluworks Ltd, a majority state-owned aluminium rolling mill, has offered five million new ordinary shares at 1,350 cedis ($0.80) each, increasing its issued shares by about 50 percent.
The offer, launched on Tuesday, is restricted to selected institutions, individuals and fund managers in Ghana and abroad, one of the co-managers said.

"The fact that it is restricted means that we do not have to come up with at least 100 new shareholders, according to the Ghana Stock Exchange Regulations," said Ken Ofori Atta of Databank Brokerage Ltd.

"We are signalling that we focus on institutional and strategic shareholders," Ofori Atta told Reuters, mentioning VALCO, Kaiser Aluminum Corp's aluminium smelter in Ghana, Ghanaian insurance firms and emerging markets funds overseas.
He said capital raised from the offer would be used to finance expansion and plant modernisation.

"With an annual capacity of 20,000 tonnes, Aluworks is the largest aluminium rolling mill in Africa outside South Africa, and one of the six aluminium rolling mills in Africa," Ghana's Minister of Employment and Social Welfare, Donald Sarpong Boateng, said at ceremony on Monday night to launch the offer.
The minister spoke on behalf of Ghana's Divestiture Implementation Committee, of which he is a member.
Aluworks will make its debut on the Ghana Stock Exchange on November 26 when it will be listed as the bourse's 21st company, ranking eighth in terms of capitalisation.
Local analysts have been bullish on the stock mainly because of the company's current quasi-monopoly status.

The Ghana government owns 45.3 percent of Aluworks, whose other main shareholders include Ghana's Social Security Bank (SSB), 17.5 percent, and the Ghana Cocoa Marketing Board (Cocobod), 8.77 percent. Staff also have a stake.

If the offer is fully subscribed the state's stake will fall to 30.48 percent, SSB's to 11.8 percent and Cocobod's to 5.89 percent. The new offering is expected to amount to 32.75 percent of the company's equity.

Aluworks had 10,266,744 ordinary shares of no par value outstanding at June 30, 1996. The net tangible book value of the company at that date was 15.3 billion cedis or 1,488 cedis per share, according to the share offer propectus.

In 1995 Aluworks produced 16,570 tonnes of aluminium products, such as sheets-in-coil, circles and roofing sheets, according to the company's share offer prospectus, compared with 16,390 tonnes in 1994.

The production is 82.5 percent of the company's installed capacity of 20,000 tonnes. More than 80 percent of its products are sold locally, with the rest exported to other West African countries, the United States and South America.
In 1995 net turnover was 53.1 billion cedis compared to 33.7 billion cedis in 1994, while profit after taxation was 3.8 billion cedis against two billion cedis in 1994.
For the first half of this year ended June 30, net turnover was 32.3 billion and profit after tax was 2.3 billion.
Long term, the company wants to double capacity to 40,000 tonnes at a cost of about $25 million, to be raised through internally generated funds and additional offerings.
